info.title: epiloYES internal HTTP API
info.summary: Public reader endpoints, editorial writes behind a bearer JWT, and the operational probes served by the Go binary.
info.description:
Machine-readable description of what the Go binary actually serves. It is written from the handlers, not from prose: where this document and `specs/001-epiloyes-alpha/contracts/http-api.md` disagree, the handlers won and this document follows them.

**Topology.** The API is not publicly routable. In every deployment (compose, Cloudflare, Kubernetes) it listens on an internal network and the Astro server is the only public HTTP surface. As defence in depth every response - this document included - carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.

**Errors.** Every handler-produced error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body: `type` (always `about:blank`), `title` (the plain rendering of the status code), `status`, and `detail` (omitted when empty). See the `Problem` schema.

**Pagination.** Lists take `limit` (default 20) and `cursor` (opaque, keyset) and answer `{ items, next_cursor }`, where `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. A `limit` outside 1-100 is rejected with 400 rather than clamped; a malformed or oversized `cursor` is rejected with 400.

**Auth.** Only the editorial endpoints require authentication: `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`, verified against the configured JWKS, and the subject's account must hold the editor role. The database enforces the same rule again on write. When `JWKS_URL` is unset the whole `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix is left unmounted deliberately, and those paths answer 404 instead of authenticating nobody.

**Unrouted paths under `/api/v1/`.** Each half of the namespace owns a catch-all. The content module answers everything under `/api/v1/` it did not route, and the editorial module answers everything under its own `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix the same way: a known path reached with the wrong method is 405 with an `Allow` header, anything else is 404, both in problem+json. The editorial prefix used to be the one corner where the router's `text/plain` answer broke the single error convention; that corner is closed, and the convention holds everywhere under `/api/v1/`.

**Completeness.** Every operation described here is served by the binary, and every route the binary registers is described here; a test in the composition root compares the two in both directions on every build.

**Availability.** The editorial routes are mounted only when the deployment configures JWKS verification; without it they answer 404 rather than authenticating nobody. The reader endpoints and the probes mount unconditionally.

servers.description: The internal service address inside compose and Kubernetes; the Astro server reaches it as API_BASE_URL.
A locally run binary (HTTP_ADDR defaults to :8080).

get.description: Answers 200 as long as the process is serving. It touches no dependency, so it never reports the database's state - that is what /readyz is for.
Pings the database. A failing ping answers 503 so an orchestrator stops routing traffic here without killing the process.

503.description: The readiness check failed; the body is the same shape, not problem+json.

get.description: Serves the committed `api/openapi.json` verbatim - the bytes are embedded into the binary at build time, so the served document and the validated file can never differ.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document describing this API.

schema.description: An OpenAPI 3.1 document - this one, byte for byte.

get.summary: Front-page feed for one language and one or more places
get.description:
Published, non-withdrawn articles, newest first, keyset-paginated on (published_at, id). Both axes are required: a reader always reads one language, and follows at least one place (repeat `place` to follow several - a diaspora reader follows two).

An article whose origin was translated renders the translation's headline and extract; an untranslated (same-language) origin renders the feed-provided title with an extract derived from the retrieved body at read time. Either way `lang` on every returned item equals the requested language.

An empty result is an empty `items` array with a 200, never an error.

400.description: Unknown `lang`, missing or unknown `place`, a `limit` outside 1-100 or a non-integer one, or a malformed `cursor`.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: unknown lang "fr": the reader languages are el and de

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: at least one place is required (repeat place= to follow several)

get.description:
The article page payload: the feed item shape plus `approved_at`.

Unknown, unpublished, withdrawn and syntactically invalid ids are one indistinguishable 404 - the existence of unpublished work is not public, so a malformed id is not even answered with a 400.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 404, not 400.

404.description: No article is visible under this id.

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no such article

get.summary: List registered sources and their poll state
get.description:
The registered feeds, newest registration first, keyset-paginated on (created_at, id), with the last poll cycle summed from each active source's poll state - so the screen's cycle numbers are readings, not invented figures.

**The licensing fields are the CURRENT row, and the payload says so.** The legal basis of anything already retrieved is the retrieval-time snapshot on `source_item` (I-4), which the provenance endpoint serves and this list deliberately does not.

`permission_evidence` is returned, behind the editor gate: the screen exists to make the licensing basis visible, and it is what separates a lawful `full_text` source from an impossible one.

Unknown and repeated query parameters are rejected with 400, like the queue's.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Filter to polled (`true`) or paused (`false`) feeds - `source.active` is the operator's pause switch, and this list is its one read path. Exactly `true` or `false`; any other value is a 400. Absent means no filter.

200.description: One page of the source list, with the last poll cycle.

400.description: Unparseable limit (outside 1-100), an `active` that is not exactly true or false, a cursor this endpoint did not issue, or an unknown or repeated query parameter.

post.description:
Registers a feed the crawler may poll. The usage rule is not an input: every new source is `extract_and_link`, and upgrades are a separate founder-gated flow outside alpha scope. Sending `usage_rule` - any value, `null` included - is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field, as is any other unknown field.

The whole `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists. Behind the gate the module's catch-all answers a wrong method with a problem+json 405 carrying `Allow`, and an unknown path with a problem+json 404, like everywhere else under `/api/v1/`.

value.name: Example Weekly
value.licence_terms: Extract and link permitted with attribution.

201.description: The source as the database recorded it.

400.description: Malformed JSON, an unknown field (`usage_rule` included), a blank required field, a `url` that is not an absolute http(s) URL with a host, or a language code the database does not know.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: usage_rule is not accepted: new sources are always extract_and_link; upgrades are a separate founder-gated flow

unfetchableURL.summary: A URL the crawler could never poll

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: url must be an absolute http or https URL with a host, e.g. https://example.org/feed.xml

409.description: A source with this feed URL is already registered.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: a source with this feed URL is already registered

get.summary: List origins awaiting an editorial decision
get.description:
Retrieved items and their translations that have no non-withdrawn article. Origins whose only articles were withdrawn reappear here as correction candidates, carrying their withdrawal history.

The whole /api/v1/editorial/ prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Optional filter: only origins whose translation targets this language, plus untranslated origins in it.

400.description: Unparseable limit (outside 1-100), malformed lang, a cursor this endpoint did not issue, or an unrecognised query parameter.

403.description: The account is not an editor.

post.summary: Approve an origin, optionally publishing it
post.description:
Approval creates the article; this endpoint carries the intent and the database enforces the rules.

**403 and 409 are the database's verdicts.** The insert trigger raises when the approver does not hold the editor role - the HTTP gate checked already, so a 403 here means the role changed under the request. The 409 comes from the one-per-origin unique indexes, with no application pre-check in front of them: a pre-check would disagree with the database exactly under the concurrency that makes the answer matter.

**Withdrawn origins may be approved again.** Those indexes are partial on `withdrawn_at IS NULL`, so an origin whose only articles are withdrawn is free - that is the documented correction flow, not a loophole.

**Side effects.** `article.approved`, and `article.published` when `publish` is true, are written to the append-only domain event stream in the same transaction as the article itself.

translated.summary: Approve a translation and publish it now

untranslated.summary: Approve a same-language item, releasing it later

400.description: Malformed JSON or an unknown field; both or neither origin supplied; an origin id that is not a UUID or names nothing; a blank attribution; or an untranslated origin whose feed provided no title, which would leave nothing to render as a headline.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: supply translation_id or source_item_id, not both: an article has exactly one origin

titlelessOrigin.summary: An untranslated item with no title

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: this item's feed provided no title, so an untranslated approval would have no headline; approve a translation of it instead

409.description: The origin already has a non-withdrawn article. Refused by the partial unique index, so two concurrent approvals of one origin produce exactly one 201 and one 409.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this origin already has a published or approved article; withdraw it before approving a correction

post.description:
Publishes an article approved with `publish: false`. The database permits `published_at` to be set exactly once, and the statement guards on it, so two concurrent callers produce exactly one 200 and one 409.

**The actor must still be an editor at the moment of the write.** This is the one editorial write no trigger can guard - nothing on the article row records who released it - so the publishing transaction takes a locking read of the actor's account row and the UPDATE itself carries the editor predicate. A demotion and a publication therefore serialize rather than race, and a demoted account gets 403 with nothing published.

**Side effect.** `article.published` in the same transaction.

An article that was approved and never released stays that way permanently unless this endpoint is called: a frozen record of an approval, which withdrawal does not apply to.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 here - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

400.description: The `{id}` path segment is not a UUID.

malformedID.summary: A path id that is not a UUID

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: the article id in the path must be a uuid

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no article with this id

409.description: The article is already published. Publication is one-way and happens once.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this article is already published; publication happens once and is never repeated

post.summary: End a publication, preserving every record
post.description:
Withdrawal ends publication and destroys nothing (FR-016, I-5). The article row, its approval, its approver, its attribution and the retrieved evidence stay exactly as they were; there is deliberately no way to erase an approval.

**One guarded statement.** The update requires the article to be published and not yet withdrawn, so two concurrent withdrawals produce exactly one 200 and one 409 and neither meets the database's exception - the loser simply matches no row.

**The origin comes back.** The one-per-origin indexes are partial on `withdrawn_at IS NULL`, so a withdrawn article frees its origin and it reappears in the review queue flagged as a correction candidate, carrying this withdrawal in its history.

**Side effect.** `article.withdrawn`, carrying who and why, written by a database trigger in the same statement - so the audit record cannot be lost to application discipline, and the endpoint emits none of its own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

400.description: Malformed JSON or an unknown field, a blank reason, or an `{id}` path segment that is not a UUID.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: reason is required and must not be blank: a withdrawal is part of the audit record, and an unexplained one explains nothing

404.description: No article with this id, or one that was never published - withdrawal ends a publication, and an approval that was never released has none. Both answer 404: the existence of unpublished work is not something this endpoint confirms either.

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no article with this id

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no published article with this id

409.description: The article is already withdrawn. Withdrawal is one-way and final: who withdrew it, when and why is frozen once recorded.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this article is already withdrawn; withdrawal is one-way and final, and who withdrew it, when and why is frozen

get.summary: The five-minute audit of one article
get.description:
The full provenance chain (US5, FR-010), answered from the `article_provenance` view in a single query (I-5): source identity, the retrieval evidence with its licence snapshots, translation lineage with its recorded cost, the named approver, publication, and any withdrawal - audit sees full history, so withdrawn articles answer too.

**The legal basis is the snapshots.** `source_item` carries the licence terms, usage rule and permission evidence exactly as they applied at retrieval, written by trigger in the same transaction as the content (I-2, I-4). The `source` object is identity only; the mutable source row is never the legal basis of anything already retrieved.

**Events.** The article's rows of the append-only `domain_event` stream (FR-012), oldest first, each carrying the recorded payload as its detail. They arrive in the same statement as the chain - one round trip, one snapshot.

parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

value.detail: the article id in the path must be a uuid

bearerAuth.description: A JWT from the auth provider, verified against the configured JWKS. The subject must map to an account holding the editor role; the database enforces the same rule again on write.

Place.name: place
Place.description: Place slug to follow. Repeat the parameter to follow several places in one feed (`?place=thessaloniki&place=berlin`).

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Absent means the default; anything that is not an integer in 1-100 is rejected with 400 rather than clamped.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque page cursor: pass back the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Its encoding is an implementation detail and may change; clients must treat it as bytes. Values over 256 characters, or ones that do not decode, are rejected with 400.

Unauthenticated.description: No bearer token, or one that is invalid, expired or belongs to no account.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer realm="editorial"`, with `error="invalid_token"` appended when a token was supplied but rejected.

value.title: Unauthorized
value.detail: a bearer token is required

NotEditor.description: The token authenticated, but the account behind it does not hold the editor role.

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: the editor role is required

InternalError.description: The request failed for a reason the caller cannot act on. Internals stay in the log: the body carries no database or stack detail, and `detail` may be absent entirely.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, as every handler in this API writes them.

type.description: Always `about:blank`, which per RFC 9457 makes `title` the plain rendering of the status code. No problem-type URIs are minted for this API.

title.description: The HTTP status text, e.g. `Bad Request`.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of this occurrence. Omitted when the server has nothing safe to say (notably on 500).

Health.title: Health
Health.description: The probe body. Not problem+json, even on 503: the probes predate the API surface and answer their own shape.

FeedItem.title: FeedItem
FeedItem.description: One published article as the reader surface renders it. Extract-and-link only: never the full body, always the outbound `source_url`.

id.description: The article id; the path parameter of the article endpoint.

headline.description: The translation's headline, or the feed-provided title for an untranslated origin.

extract.description: The translation's extract, or one derived from the retrieved body at read time for an untranslated origin. May be empty when the feed carried no usable body.

lang.description: Language of the rendered text: the translation's target locale, or the source's language for an untranslated origin. On the front page it always equals the requested `lang`.

places.description: Slugs of every place the article is tagged to, sorted; an untagged article carries an empty array rather than null.

attribution.description: The composed attribution block, rendered verbatim.

source_url.description: The original article at the publisher - the outbound link.

Article.title: Article
Article.description: The article page payload: a feed item plus the moment an editor approved it.

approved_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC. Approval precedes publication and is never erased.

FrontPage.title: FrontPage
FrontPage.description: One page of the feed. Both fields are always present.

items.description: Newest first. Empty when nothing is published for the requested axes.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

NewSource.title: NewSource
NewSource.description: A source registration. Unknown fields are rejected, so a misspelled key is a 400 rather than a silent omission.

name.description: The publication's name, as attribution will render it. Must not be blank.

url.description: The feed URL the crawler polls. Must be an absolute http or https URL carrying a host; it is also the uniqueness key for a source.

language.description: The language the source publishes in; must exist in the language reference table.

jurisdiction.description: The legal jurisdiction the source publishes under.

licence_terms.description: The terms under which this material may be reused, recorded verbatim for the audit trail.

usage_rule.description: Always `extract_and_link` for a newly registered source - the endpoint does not accept any other value.

ListedSource.title: ListedSource
ListedSource.description: One registered source as the list shows it. The licensing fields are the CURRENT source row - the legal basis of anything already retrieved is the snapshot on `source_item` (I-4), served by the provenance endpoint, never by this list.

url.description: The feed URL the crawler polls - the same column the registration wrote, under one name across both source endpoints.

licence_terms.description: The terms currently on record - not the terms that applied to any given retrieval.

permission_evidence.description: The recorded written permission behind a full_text rule, or null when none is on record. Served behind the editor gate, deliberately: the list exists to make the licensing basis visible.

active.description: Whether the crawler currently polls this feed - the operator's pause switch, observable here and nowhere else.

last_polled_at.description: When the poll loop last completed an attempt, success or failure alike; null for a feed never polled.

PollCycle.title: PollCycle
PollCycle.description: The last poll cycle, summed from each ACTIVE source's poll-state columns - real readings, never invented figures. Paused sources are excluded: their state describes a poll no longer running.

retrieved.description: How many new items the last poll of each active source stored, summed.

duplicates_skipped.description: How many items the content fingerprint recognised as already on record (FR-014), summed.

failures.description: The names of the active feeds whose last poll failed, sorted by name; [] (never null) when every last poll succeeded.

SourceList.title: SourceList
SourceList.description: One page of the source list, with the last poll cycle beside it. All three fields are always present.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. null on the last page - an absent cursor always means the list is exhausted.

Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
Withdrawal.description: One ended publication in an origin's history. Withdrawal preserves every record (FR-016), so the entry stays queryable for good.

QueueItem.title: QueueItem
QueueItem.description: One origin awaiting an editorial decision: a retrieved item, with its translation when one exists. translation_id and the translated fields are null together, for an untranslated origin.

headline_original.description: source_item.original_title - null when the feed provided none.

licence_snapshot.description: The licence terms in force when this item was retrieved (I-4), not the source row today.

correction_candidate.description: True exactly when withdrawals is non-empty: the origin is back in the queue because its only articles were withdrawn, so the editor is looking at a correction rather than a first approval.

withdrawals.description: Newest first; [] (never null) for a fresh origin.

ReviewQueue.title: ReviewQueue
ReviewQueue.description: One page of the review queue. Both fields are always present.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. null on the last page - an absent cursor always means the queue is exhausted.

NewApproval.title: NewApproval
NewApproval.description: An editorial decision to publish. Exactly one origin: `translation_id` for a translated article, `source_item_id` for an untranslated one, mirroring the database's `article_exactly_one_origin`. Supplying both, neither, or an explicit `null` for both is a 400. The approver is always the authenticated editor and is deliberately not a field here.

source_item_id.description: The retrieved item being approved untranslated. Its `original_title` becomes the headline, so an item whose feed provided no title is refused with 400.

attribution.description: The attribution block rendered with the article, pointing back to the original publisher. Stored trimmed; never blank.

publish.description: Publish in the same transaction as the approval. When false the article is an approved record awaiting release.

places.description: Place slugs the article publishes to - the front page is scoped by place, so an article tagged to no place can never appear on any of them, and the database refuses such an article at commit. An unknown or repeated slug is a 400 naming it, and so is a blank slug - empty or whitespace-only; minLength catches only the former, the server refuses both.

Approval.title: Approval
Approval.description: The article the approval created. A row in `article` IS the approval (I-1): there is no draft state, and no path creates one without a named editor.

approved_by.description: The authenticated editor who approved it.

published_at.description: When publication began, or null on the `publish: false` path.

NewWithdrawal.title: NewWithdrawal
NewWithdrawal.description: The decision to end a publication. Only the reason is supplied: who withdrew it comes from the bearer token, never from the body.

reason.description: Why publication is ending. Part of the audit record, so a blank one is refused - an unexplained withdrawal explains nothing. Stored trimmed.

WithdrawalRecord.title: WithdrawalRecord
WithdrawalRecord.description: The recorded withdrawal. The article row, its approval, its attribution and the retrieved evidence all survive it (FR-016, I-5).

withdrawn_by.description: The authenticated editor who ended the publication.

reason.description: The justification as the database froze it into `article.withdrawal_reason` - guarded all-or-none with the other withdrawal columns and permanent once written. The record, not an echo of the request; never blank.

ArticleProvenance.title: ArticleProvenance
ArticleProvenance.description: The full audit chain of one article, from the `article_provenance` view in one query (I-5). The `source` object is identity only: the legal basis always comes from the retrieval-time snapshots inside `source_item` (I-4).

headline.description: The translation's headline, or the item's original title for an article published untranslated - the same resolution the reader sees.

places.description: Where the article published to, as sorted place slugs. Always a list, never null.

translation.description: The translation lineage, or null for an article published untranslated.

published_at.description: When publication began, or null for an approved-but-never-released record.

withdrawal.description: How publication ended, or null while it has not.

events.description: The article's rows of the append-only audit stream (FR-012), oldest first. Always a list, never null.

ProvenanceSource.title: ProvenanceSource
ProvenanceSource.description: The licensed feed's identity - and identity ONLY. No licence field belongs here: the source row is mutable, and the legal basis of what was retrieved is the immutable snapshots on `source_item` (I-4).

ProvenanceSourceItem.title: ProvenanceSourceItem
ProvenanceSourceItem.description: The immutable retrieval record (I-2, I-3): what was fetched, when, its database-computed fingerprint, and the licence terms exactly as they applied at retrieval, written by trigger in the same transaction as the content (I-4).

source_url.description: The original article at the publisher.

original_title.description: The item title exactly as the feed provided it, or null when it omitted one.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the retrieved body, computed by the database.

licence_snapshot.description: The licence terms as they applied at retrieval (I-4).

usage_rule_snapshot.description: The usage rule in force at retrieval.

permission_evidence_snapshot.description: The permission evidence on record at retrieval, or null when there was none.

original_author.description: The author as the feed named them, or null when it did not.

ProvenanceTranslation.title: ProvenanceTranslation
ProvenanceTranslation.description: The machine-translation lineage (FR-005): which model, which prompt version, when, and the provider-reported cost recorded at insert (FR-006).

ProvenanceApproval.title: ProvenanceApproval
ProvenanceApproval.description: The named human whose decision the article is (I-1).

ProvenanceWithdrawal.title: ProvenanceWithdrawal
ProvenanceWithdrawal.description: The recorded end of publication (FR-016): who, when and why, frozen once written.

ProvenanceEvent.title: ProvenanceEvent
ProvenanceEvent.description: One row of the append-only audit stream (FR-012). The detail is the recorded payload itself, compact, minus the article_id the response is already scoped to - the record, never a paraphrase.
